title: Check yourself: The calendar, the audit and the settings a new model changes

questions.stem: A deprecation table lists one of a company's models with a retirement of "not sooner than" a date nine weeks away. How should the team treat that entry?

options.text: Plan against it as the earliest cut-off and begin early, since it slips later, not earlier
options.says: The table can say "not sooner than" for a model that is still active, which marks a date that may move later.

options.text: Wait for the vendor to confirm a final cut-off before spending any effort on the move
options.says: Ruled out because "is never a date to wait for".

options.text: Treat it as a fixed cut-off that cannot move, and schedule the whole migration to end on that day
options.says: Ruled out because "marks a date that may move later".

options.text: Ignore it until the status changes to retired, because nothing breaks before that point
options.says: Ruled out because "Deprecated models are likely to be less reliable than active models", so nothing is safe until the retired state.

questions.stem: A model's entry in the documentation carries the status legacy. What does that status say?

options.text: It has a retirement date and will fail on that day, so requests must already be moved
options.says: Ruled out because deprecated is the state where Anthropic "provides a recommended replacement and assigns a retirement date".

options.text: It is the recommended choice for new work, since only deprecated models are withdrawn
options.says: Ruled out because active is the state where "The model is fully supported and recommended for use".

options.text: It stops receiving updates and heads toward deprecation, so plan the move before any date is set
options.says: Legacy means "The model will no longer receive updates and may be deprecated in the future."

options.text: It has been retired already, so every request that names it comes back as a failure
options.says: Ruled out because "Requests to retired models will fail" describes the retired state, not legacy.
